persona_mapping: Champion contact / MD / owner-operator / nominated administrator
description: Genuinely administrative: users, roles, workspaces, organisation settings, approval routing and guardrail defaults (both under rule R17), audit access and restore requests. Holds no proposal authorship, cost administration, catalogue writes, approval or implementation rights. A champion who also prices holds Pricing Manager as a second role under rule R4, which keeps the administrative and commercial planes separate in the audit trail.

Core daily user. Creates, edits and submits proposals and pricing rules, maintains the catalogue within scope, uses AI assistance, requests overrides, sets initial effective dates. Cannot approve, cannot implement, cannot alter guardrails.
Draft tier. Creates and edits drafts of proposals and rules, uses AI assistance, comments. Cannot submit by default (per-organisation toggle, open decision D3). Cost visibility off by default.

persona_mapping: Sales, operations, procurement, customer service or GTM staff
description: Cross-functional intake lane. Comments, attaches evidence and raises structured price-change requests (items, direction, reason, supporting signal) without any pricing authority: no drafts, no cost or margin data, no submission, no approval. Distinct from Viewer, which reads decisions but cannot contribute; the Contributor contributes but does not read proposals.

Approves, rejects and requests changes within configured magnitude thresholds. Owns margin and cost guardrails and cost data. Approves overrides subject to the identity check. Does not create or edit proposals.

Same approval verbs as Finance Approver; guardrail domain is commercial policy: MAP, parity, channel and regional rules. Also reviews vendor-scoped proposals (third-party seller prices entered on the seller's behalf by internal staff) — no separate Vendor Manager role exists; this is a routing choice on the same approve step, not a new capability. Frequently dual-assigned with other roles in smaller pilot companies.

Final tier above the top magnitude threshold or for items flagged strategic, and the arbiter when the finance and commercial domains disagree. Approve and reject only, plus dashboards. Deliberately has no edit rights.

Records implementation of approved changes only: marks approved items implemented, manages post-approval scheduling. Distinct checkpoint from approval (adopted from the CTO breakdown). Small pilots may merge this with Pricing Manager by dual assignment.
Read-only on assigned workspaces: proposals, statuses, published prices, policy guardrails. No cost or margin data unless the visibility flag is set. No comments.

Reads everything within the tenant, writes nothing: full audit trails, version history, decision rationale, override records, audit pack export. Cannot comment, to avoid influencing decisions under review.

Attributed principal. Generates drafts, summaries, scenarios and risk flags when invoked. Inherits the invoking user's scope and cost visibility, never exceeding them. All output enters the workflow as drafts or comments credited to the AI. Hard-denied submit, approve and implement.
